meta_description: Old Dubai souk tours compared on price, food tastings, abra ride, Emirati house visit and pickup. From €11 to €29, 2 to 6 hours. Find your tour fast.

lead: For most people the best Old Dubai tour is the €20 Old Town, Abra Cruise, Museums and Souks tour: 2.5–4 hours from Al Seef through Al Fahidi, a private abra across the Creek, museum entry, 4 tastings and a briefing on real souk prices before you haggle, with guides in 7 languages. Only have 2 hours? The 4.93-rated small-group tour (€25) fits 6 tastings into a loop that ends where it starts.

Almost every tour walks the same line: Al Fahidi's wind-tower houses, an abra across Dubai Creek, then the Spice and Gold Souks in Deira. What separates them is how much food is really in the price (from none to 8 street-food items), whether an Emirati house or museum is included, and where you start: a metro exit, a heritage café or your hotel lobby.
The common trap: several tours put shawarma and falafel in the name but serve them only on the premium option. The table below shows what each from-price really buys, from €11 to €29.

review: This is the tour to book if you only do Old Dubai once. For €20 you get the full classic loop: Al Seef and the coral-stone wind-tower houses of Al Fahidi, the Grand Souk in Bur Dubai, a private abra across Dubai Creek and then the Spice and Gold Souks in Deira, with museum and heritage-site entry included. No other tour on this page combines all of that at this price.

What sets it apart is the souk briefing. Before each market the guide stops to explain real prices, haggling and the common vendor tactics, then lets you shop on your own. If you plan to buy spices, a pashmina or gold, that briefing is worth more than the tastings.

The catch is the food. The base price covers Arabic coffee and tea, dates, Dubai chocolate and camel milk chocolate; the shawarma, falafel and fresh juices in the headline belong to the premium option. If street food is the point of your evening, compare it with #4, which puts eight food items in the base price.

review: If you have a free morning or late afternoon rather than a whole evening, this is the one. In 2 to 2.5 hours it covers Bastakiya and the old Emirati houses, Al Seef, an abra across Dubai Creek and the Spice and Gold Souks, then brings you back to the Arabian Tea House in Al Fahidi, so there is no taxi to find in Deira afterwards.

It also has the best guest score of the big tours here, 4.93, and the most generous sweet-and-tea line-up: Arabic coffee, saffron tea, dates, chocolates, local sweets and iced tea, plus a spices experience and entry to Baba's Cave.

Two trade-offs. At €25 for about 2 hours it is the priciest walking tour per hour (roughly €10–13), and the souk stops are brief in the itinerary, about 10 minutes each. If your main goal is shopping time in the Gold Souk, #7 gives you around 45 minutes there.

review: This is the original Al Khayma route, and it is built around a sit-down start: 30 minutes inside a historic Emirati house with Arabic coffee, dates and snacks and a gallery of old UAE photographs, before you walk Al Seef, Al Fahidi Fort and the Bur Dubai Souk and cross the Creek by abra.

In Deira you get roughly 30 minutes each in the Spice Souk and Gold Souk, enough for real shopping, plus the guide's spice and souvenir tips. At a €22 from-price it adds five guide languages (English, French, German, Italian, Spanish) and a hotel pickup option.

Read the options carefully. At the from-price the food is coffee or tea, dates and camel milk chocolate. The street-food line-up (karak and samosa, shawarma and falafel, luqaimat, camel milk ice cream) is marked Premium Tour. The same route is sold as a premium street-food tour at €29 and a €16 basic version, so pick the tier you actually want.

review: This is the pick if you do not want to deal with the metro or taxis. For €25 you are collected from your hotel and get Old Dubai (the Gold and Spice Souks, an abra across the Creek, Bastakiya and Al Khayma Heritage House with Arabic tea and coffee) plus the new city: a Palm Jumeirah drive, a Marina walk, Burj Al Arab and Museum of the Future photo stops and a guided visit to the Blue Mosque.

The Dubai Frame is the useful extra. Book the Frame option and the day ends with about an hour at the Frame, looking over old and new Dubai; without it, the Frame is a photo stop and you go back to the hotel. If you also want the Burj Khalifa deck, compare Burj Khalifa tickets separately, because no tour here includes them.

The trade-off is depth. With so many stops, Bastakiya gets about 20 minutes and there are no food tastings beyond tea and coffee. For more classic half-day tours with pickup, see our Dubai city tours comparison.

review: If the souks are why you are going, this tour gives you the most time in them: about 45 minutes in the Spice Souk and 45 in the Gold Souk, versus 10 to 30 minutes on most tours here. Before that you get 45 minutes in Bastakiya, the Old Textile Market and the Grand Souk, and an abra water taxi across the Creek.

It suits shoppers more than history fans: there is no heritage house or museum entry on the included list, and guides speak English or German only.

review: A no-frills Old Dubai walk that does the essentials well for €17, with all entry fees and taxes included. It starts with the guide meeting you at Sharaf DG Metro, Exit 4, walks Al Seef and Bastakiya, stops at the Bayt Al Khanyar Museum and Coffee Shop, then crosses the Creek by shared abra for 30 minutes each in the Spice and Gold Souks.

It is new, with only 4 reviews, so it ranks below the proven tours.

guide.h2: Old Dubai Tours Compared Side by Side
guide.html:
All ten tours cross Dubai Creek by abra and visit the Spice and Gold Souks. What changes is the price, the length, how much food sits in the base price, whether an Emirati house or museum is included, the group format and where you meet. Prices are adult from-prices in euros; per-hour figures divide the price by the listed length.

Three numbers stand out. #1 at €20 is the cheapest tour that combines museum entry, a private abra and a pickup option. #4 at €29 is the only one with a full street-food line-up (8 items) in the base price. And per hour, #10 at about €2.80 is the cheapest guided walk, while #6 at about €4–5 is the cheapest way to get hotel pickup included, though much of its 5–6 hours is spent driving between stops.

guide.h2: The Al Khayma Route: Which of the Three Tiers to Book
guide.html:
Three tours here start at the same place, Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant in Al Fahidi, and walk the same route: the heritage house, Al Seef, Al Fahidi Fort, Bur Dubai Souk, the abra, and the Spice and Gold Souks. The difference is the food:

  • #5 from €16: coffee or tea, dates and camel milk chocolate; karak tea and samosa as an option. Ages 5+.
  • #3 from €22: the same base tastings, five guide languages including French, and a Premium Tour option that adds the full street-food list.
  • #4 from €29: shawarma, falafel, karak tea, samosa, rogag, luqaimat, camel milk ice cream and lemon mint juice already included.

If you will eat dinner on the tour, book #4. If not, #5 shows you the same sights for about €12 less.

guide.h2: Which Old Dubai Tour Should You Book?
guide.html:
• First visit, one tour only: #1 Old Town, Abra, Museums & Souks. €20, private abra, museum entry, price briefing before each souk, 7 languages.
  • Only 2 hours free: #2. 4.93 rated, 6 tastings, starts and ends at the Arabian Tea House.
  • Street food as dinner: #4 Premium Street Food, 8 items in the price.
  • Cheapest with an Emirati house: #5 at €16.
  • No metro, no taxis: #6 with hotel pickup, the Blue Mosque and a Dubai Frame option.
  • Serious souk shopping: #7, about 45 minutes each in the Spice and Gold Souks.
  • Hindi or Urdu-speaking guide on a budget: #8 at €17.
  • History and museums: #9 with the Coin Museum.
  • After dark, lowest price: #10 Evening Heritage Walk at €11.

Want Old Dubai as part of a wider sightseeing day with Downtown and the Palm? Compare the best Dubai city tours instead.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Getting There, What to Bring and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Getting there

The walking tours start on the Bur Dubai side of the Creek. Sharaf DG Metro (Green Line), Exit 4 is the meeting point for #7 and #8 and the nearest station for #9 at Al Seef. Several tours end in Deira near Al Ras Metro, so you can take the metro back rather than a taxi. Only #6 includes hotel pickup as standard; #1, #3, #4, #7 and #8 offer it as an option, #2 only on its private version.

What to bring

Comfortable shoes, a sun hat and sunglasses are on almost every tour's list. Baby strollers and large bags are not allowed on #3 and #7, and #4 and #5 do not take large bags either, so leave shopping bags at the hotel. Most of these walks are not suitable for wheelchair users or people with limited mobility; the vehicle-based #6 involves the least walking.

What costs extra

Tips are listed as extra on most tours. Watch the options: shawarma and falafel on #1 and #3, karak tea and samosa on #5, and the Dubai Frame ticket on #6 all depend on what you select at booking. Anything you buy in the souks is extra, which is why #1's price briefing earns its keep.

Making a day or a stay of it

Old Dubai pairs well with an evening dinner cruise, and the desert is a separate half day (see our desert safaris comparison). To wake up next to the souks, compare the best hotels on Dubai Creek or the heritage-style boutique hotels in Dubai.

faqs.q: What is the best Old Dubai tour?
faqs.a: For most visitors, the Old Town, Abra Cruise, Museums, Souks and Street Food Tour from €20: 2.5–4 hours through Al Fahidi and the Spice and Gold Souks, with a private abra, museum entry, 4 tastings and 7 guide languages. If you only have 2 hours, the 4.93-rated small-group tasting tour from the Arabian Tea House (€25) is the better fit.

faqs.q: Which Dubai street food tour includes the most food?
faqs.a: The Old Dubai Premium Guided Tour with Street Food (from €29) includes shawarma, falafel, karak tea, samosa, rogag, luqaimat, camel milk ice cream and lemon mint juice, plus coffee and dates, all in the base price. On several other tours the shawarma and falafel are only on the premium option.

faqs.q: Is the abra ride included on Old Dubai tours?
faqs.a: Yes, on all ten tours compared here the abra across Dubai Creek is included. Tour #1 uses a private abra with priority boarding; #8 uses a shared one.

faqs.q: How long is an Old Dubai souk tour?
faqs.a: Walking tours run 2 to 4 hours. The shortest is 2–2.5 hours (#2), most are about 3 hours, and the hotel-pickup tour with the Blue Mosque and Dubai Frame takes 5–6 hours including driving.

faqs.q: Do Old Dubai tours include hotel pickup?
faqs.a: Only the Creek, Souks, Blue Mosque and Frame tour includes hotel pickup as standard (not from Jebel Ali, Discovery Gardens, Investment Park, Expo City or Silicon Oasis). Several walking tours offer pickup as an option; the rest meet at Al Fahidi, Al Seef or Sharaf DG Metro, Exit 4.

faqs.q: Is there an evening Old Dubai tour?
faqs.a: Yes: the Evening Heritage Walk from €11 meets at Marsa Al Seef, crosses the Creek by abra and visits the Gold and Spice Souks over about 4 hours. It includes no food or museum tickets, so eat before or after.

faqs.q: Are Old Dubai walking tours suitable for kids and wheelchair users?
faqs.a: Most are not suitable for wheelchair users or people with limited mobility. Age limits vary: the Al Khayma tours (#3, #4) exclude under-2s and the €16 version (#5) excludes under-5s; strollers are not allowed on #3 and #7.

methodology: We compared 10 bookable Old Dubai tours that cover Al Fahidi, the abra across Dubai Creek and the Deira souks, from an €11 evening walk to a 6-hour tour with hotel pickup. Each was scored on price and price per hour, length, food tastings in the base price, abra type, Emirati house or museum entry, group format, start time and meeting point or pickup. Prices are live from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews.
